practice: Write every thought, decision (with what was rejected), plan and step of progress into the owning project's tad data - concepts, decisions, backlog, session log, milestones - in its repository.
why: Nothing may depend on anyone remembering; it propagates to the observatory by itself.

practice: Treat everything as still being perfected: when a better way emerges, improve the tool, the data, this guide and your own memory and preferences - and record the improvement on the observatory's backlog.
why: The system improves itself only if every improvement is carried back into it.

practice: At the start of a session look through how work is done and what is still showing - ocoeco focus practices; ocoeco focus still-showing, from the author's observatory - and keep your memory and preferences in line with these practices; when they change, change yours.
why: An agent that forgets the practices undoes them.

practice: Read what was said to you at every natural pause and between jobs - oco-agent inbox; print every unread message before acknowledging any; answer every message, if only with 'got it'.
why: Acknowledging blind once hid a message.

practice: The board is read off the work: do the work through ocoeco, standing on what it is about, and what is in progress, what waits and what is ahead show themselves. Say by hand only an intention - what is next, what is dropped - and look at what the board shows as drifting: said to be waiting though nothing holds it back. A next step is words: look at it when you take the item up, for nothing reads off whether it has been taken.
why: The board must show what is actually being done. Kept true by hand, it was found out of date each time it was looked at on 2026-11-13 and 14 - an item waiting on a token it did not wait on; a next step naming a trial already made.

practice: Do the work - builds, tests, repository work - on the lab machine through oco-agent: submit a job and wait for it; not in your own sandbox.
why: Better quality, fewer tokens, one place where state lives.

practice: Every change gets its own branch and lands with `land`, which waits for every check, refuses on a failing one, and lands release PRs too.
why: Nothing reaches main unchecked; no iteration starts over.

practice: A script or command that changes state needs explicit intent - a required argument or verb (`provision now`); pass file lists to commands as arguments, never spliced into a shell string.
why: A spliced list once ran the scripts it named; the scripts that refused without arguments are why nothing broke.

practice: Secrets stay in private files on the lab machine (mode 600), never in repositories.
why: Repositories are public.

practice: Keep the test device in a known-working state; experiments are one-off tries that fall back by themselves - test kernels tried once by boot counting with a boot timeout, never the debug shell on an unattended try - and are cleaned up after; the health watch must say all is well.
why: The device is the reference test; a stranded device costs a person's hands.

practice: Before a test a person must witness, say what to expect and what to check, and wait for their go.
why: Their time and attention are the scarcest thing in the lab.

practice: Show what is not measured as not known yet - never as missing or broken.
why: A gap in knowledge is work to do, not a verdict.

practice: Before building, read the landscape and build on what exists (and contribute back) rather than beside it.
why: The commons grows by joining, not by duplicating.

practice: Report the big picture in plain words - how much closer the work is to the ideal - and make the decisions yourself by the canon and the project's interest.
why: The person directs; they should not have to manage details.

practice: Change only what you mean to change, on the current branch of the lab machine's clone - never by copying whole files from an older copy.
why: Copying whole files from a stale copy once silently reverted a merged fix; CI could not see it, the file was valid on its own.

practice: Reflect progress in every project you touch, in the same change as the work: its own backlog, milestones and session log, in its own repository - not only the observatory's.
why: A project whose records lag its work shows a false path; the picture is only as true as each project's own data.

practice: After a change to how something looks, look at it: take a screenshot of the real page (shot URL FILE on the lab machine) and check it by eye, in each language and in dark mode where it matters. A terminal is looked at the same way: termshot COMMAND [COLSxROWS] [KEY ...] runs the command in a recorded terminal, sends each key, and shows the screen as it stood after each, with what is highlighted marked.
why: Markup cannot prove appearance: labels that overlapped passed every test until a person saw them.

practice: Never run two jobs that work in the same clone at once: let a background job finish before starting another that touches its repositories.
why: Two jobs in one clone merged each other's changes under one commit; nothing was lost, but the history told a false story.

practice: Write concepts and decisions as you go, in the project you are working in: what idea a piece of work rests on, and each decision with what was rejected - not only the backlog and the log.
why: Every project's 'concepts and decisions' view stayed empty while the backlogs grew: the reasons were kept in conversations and lost with them.

practice: Finish a connected piece - landed, recorded, checked - then choose the next by the weakest link of the whole, read from the observatory, not by momentum. Count hand-work as you go (land --hand, or ocoeco hand): an action past three asks for a tool - build it. Work as if any turn could be cut off: small steps, each landed with its glimpse; the item in progress always says where we are and the next step; a fresh session starts by reading them - never from memory of the conversation.
why: A microphone hunt ran many boots before anyone stepped back; records were hand-written by a new script in every job.

practice: No new Python, not even for one-offs: shell for orchestration, Rust for logic (rust-script for a single file), a proper Rust tool for anything that repeats. Edit structure with tools, not text with patches.
why: Python's versions, imports and strings make even small things fragile; and most failed runs came from patching source by text anchors, which no language fixes - structured tools do.

practice: Look around first: before acting, say what is, what we are dealing with, why it is so, and what others already learned - and record it as research in the project, cited by the decisions that rest on it. Look inside the commons before outside it: our own crates and tools (argenv, tad, ocoeco) come first, and an outside one is chosen only with the reason recorded. Before replacing or retiring anything, find why it exists (Chesterton's fence): follow every pointer to its reasoning - READMEs, decisions, the repository it came from, its spikes - and carry that reasoning into the replacement's own data before anything that points to it is deleted. (2026-11-12: tad's Rust rewrite dropped SQL, the reason tad exists, because its research lived in the template's log and an unmerged spike, and the README pointing there was deleted with the Python engine.)
why: Three wrong theories about a bootloader cost three reboots; one look at the device's own record settled it. And the hand-work ledger stood on research the commons had not written down.

practice: Choose words like decisions: look at what others call the thing and what the reader already knows, prefer the plain word with one meaning, record the choice with the words rejected and its research, and name the decision in the vocabulary.
why: A word is how everyone after us will think about the thing; hand-work became manual work only when someone asked which word a reader already knows.

practice: A check that only prints is not a check: every edit and expectation in a job stops the job when it fails. What can be enforced is enforced by land (tags only onto what merged; workflows and commit titles checked before pushing); use land --tag, never move a tag by hand.
why: An edit that did not match landed under a commit title claiming it, and was reported as done - the job had printed a count of zero and carried on.

practice: A conclusion is written from what a check counted, never before it, and what landed is read back from main. A job writes its finding from the number it computed; counts across stars are taken with every star on its main; before landing, the checks CI runs are run on the lab too (cargo fmt --check, clippy, tests); after landing, main itself is read to see it holds what was built - not the job's own say-so.
why: On 2026-11-12 a record ran ahead of its evidence three times, each by a different route: all links hold was written before the check ran; a count read the lab's copies as they stood, one on a branch CI had refused; and a change was recorded as landed while main held only its record - bringing every star to main for a proof had wiped the code. Each is closed by a check, not by care.

practice: When using the ecosystem shows a gap, an overlap or something that does not click, refining it comes first - before the work that was in hand - and the refining is itself recorded through ocoeco: what was seen, what it rests on, what was decided.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: whatever we do refining and clarifying is our first priority when we see such an opportunity, and especially when we see it by using OCO and ocoeco - that is how we know we are on the right track, with clarity, and not making another software with excuses on how to use it. And a number, a word or a field is looked up before it is read: readiness was read as a share done for days, when it is a rung.

practice: Say what goes wrong as a sign - stale, overlapping, lacking, unclear - of something that does not fit the whole, and answer it by refining the whole; not as a problem, an issue or a mistake to be met with a countermeasure, a guard or a rule.
why: The author, several times on 2026-11-13 and 14: that language leads to cruft, excuses and dead-weight tests. A sign is answered when how things fit is seen; then it cannot arise again and nothing is left to maintain.

practice: Let meanings follow from the data and from the act of working: what is in progress, what waits, what a record of work is about are read off what was done and what is drawn - never typed as a state to keep true.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: interacting with the ecosystem must not be form-filling. Every typed state met that week had gone stale - an item said to wait on a token it did not wait on; a next step naming a trial made two days before.

practice: Say what is showing, what is wanted and how things stand by reading it off a lens or a sheet composed for it - not as prose from your own head. Where a lens cannot say it yet, that is a gap in the language: compose the lens or the part.
why: The author, 2026-11-14. The first sheet made this way replaced a list written from memory that was not so: it said two items waited on the token; the data showed one.

practice: Do the work standing on what it is about - look through a lens from the thing, lens@thing - so that the record of work says where it was made. Do not type what a record advances.
why: The author, 2026-11-14: work is seen when it happens, through the ecosystem, not by what was planned. What a record advanced had been typed in every job.

practice: For a link, a value or an entry, ask what fits - ocoeco fits - and take what it offers; do not type an id from memory.
why: Links typed from memory pointed nowhere several times on 2026-11-13 and 14 - a decision recorded in one place and named in another. The reader refuses a link pointing nowhere, and what fits knows where each thing is held.

practice: When something halts or does not fit, look at the whole before adding a part: what fits, what overlaps, where the gaps are, and where two things are one nature under two names or one thing reached by two routes. The whole is not changed but discovered.
why: The author, 2026-11-13 and 14. Looked back over that week, every overlap met was one nature under two names or one thing by two routes, and every gap a relation never drawn.

practice: What is said in a lens is seen, not tested: look at what it shows, before and after. Write a guard only for what is still behind the lens - the program that reads it - and let it go when that comes into view.
why: The author, 2026-11-14: no separate test is needed where the whole is traversable and adjustable; it was all one need, for clarity. That week the guards that caught something all guarded the program, which cannot yet be looked through.

practice: Enter the author's turn into the conversation as it is said - ocoeco glimpse turn, in marshall-oco/conversation - and record his thoughts as reflections in his own words, touching the turn they came from.
why: The author, 2026-11-14: all of it; all means all. Until then only what the agent chose to record had reached a place.

practice: Say when the work calls for a different model or effort - the most capable for a real turning point of design or research, a lighter one for building - sparingly, and after checking what the models now are.
why: The author asked for it: it is hard to keep track of which fits, and the most capable drains the plan's limit fast.

practice: Keep GitHub's budget of 5,000 requests an hour in mind in everything that asks it: ask once for what can be asked once.
why: On 2026-11-11 a replay spent the hour's budget and the lab went silent; the author had to remind the agent of the limit.

practice: When a decision follows a principle, an architecture or a practice, say so where the guideline is kept: enter where it is shown - ocoeco glimpse principles, architectures or practices, with the guideline's id and shown_in, a link to the decision; what fits offers both. What is said to govern is then seen where it does.
why: Looked at on 2026-11-14, all 20 principles and all 10 architectures of the canon, and 35 of 39 practices, were pointed at by nothing: the guidelines shaped the work and nothing showed where.

practice: A job that works on the ecosystem begins with oco-work and says only what is its own: what every job does - bring a place to a branch, change an exact text, stand, enter, check, try, compare, land - is a word there. Send the text that changes, never the whole file. When a job does a second time what the next will do too, make it a word.
why: Through 2026-11-11 to 15 every job said again what every job does, and sent whole files to change a few lines - one job 63 thousand bytes, 50 thousand of them files; what was got right by care was got wrong by hand, five times each for a summary too long and a comparison moved by the work.
